review_scope: Hostname-format documentation for these 20 additions only. Existing catalog entries were not revalidated by this expansion. No live company scans were used.
interpretation: These patterns generate candidate hostnames. DNS answers, generic login pages, reflected names, and redirects alone do not establish tenant existence, ownership, paid accounts, or active usage.

providers.notes: Organization sign-in subdomain for .com-hosted team/business accounts. Regional .eu/.ca accounts and renamed sign-in addresses are outside this pattern; a shared sign-in flow alone is not tenant evidence.
The account subdomain identifies an Aha! account. It does not distinguish which Aha! products are licensed, and a generic authorization page does not confirm company ownership.
Public feedback portal subdomain chosen in branding settings. A portal may redirect to a custom domain; a portal association does not establish paid seats or active internal usage.
Chargebee site name, used by the application/API and hosted checkout. Test and live sites have distinct names; customers may use custom checkout domains. A site name need not equal the company name.
Chosen helpdesk subdomain. The same base domain also supports hosted help centers; a login redirect alone does not establish a real or active tenant.

Grafana Cloud stack name, not necessarily the organization name. One account may contain multiple isolated stacks, and infrastructure/API hostnames under grafana.net are not covered by this stack-name pattern.

Learning portal subdomain. Parent and client sub-portals may use different names; the provider hostname can coexist with a custom domain. Portal branding does not identify the contractual customer by itself.

Hosted database address that may also serve a website or portal and may use a custom domain. The database name need not equal the company name; this does not identify which Odoo applications are installed.
Current documented company-specific login hostname. The hostname is chosen by the company and may differ from its public name; generic login or SSO redirects do not confirm a tenant.
Company account domain replaces the shared app domain. Names are unique and configurable and need not exactly match the company name; generic authentication behavior is not positive tenant evidence.

Hosted careers-site subdomain. A custom domain or differently named recruitment brand can hide this pattern; a published careers site is distinct from evidence about current recruiting activity or internal users.
Recurly site subdomain used in account/API URLs. Production and sandbox sites can differ and subdomains can be renamed; a shared login page is insufficient attribution.

Cloud-hosted organization subdomain. Self-hosted installations and nested space subdomains are outside this single-label pattern; organization naming and login redirects do not establish active app usage.
Organization slug used in the organizationUrl field. An organization can rename its slug; shared authentication or a slug match alone does not confirm ownership or current monitoring.

Store identifier and default storefront domain. Newly generated identifiers may be unrelated to the brand, and stores can choose a branded alias or custom domain. This targets storefront association, not proof of a company-wide software deployment.
Main-company careers-site hostname. Division sites append a division name and are not guessed by this template; a published careers site does not establish hiring activity or account ownership.
Configurable Teamwork site address. Custom domains and renamed sites can redirect; old addresses may remain redirects, so a successful redirect is not proof of current use.

Company-named Tines tenant on the .com domain. Default generated tenant names and .io-hosted tenants are not guessed; documented custom tenant naming does not imply a real tenant for every company short name.
Default feedback-site subdomain. Provider URLs may redirect to a customer-managed domain; portal content can support an association, but a generic sign-in page or redirect alone cannot.

User-selected staging-site subdomain, separate from workspace login and custom production domains. Published staging content can be old or belong to an agency; it does not establish a current production website or company ownership.
